chunk_findings.detail: The new `history` parameter is declared `cli_only=True`, so it is not exposed to the MCP `show` action. An MCP client that requests the `show` action cannot set `history=true`; the action call therefore always evaluates `bool(a.get("history"))` as false and the returned view can only show the latest correction per field, not the full correction list. This contradicts the stated acceptance/four-way configurability requirement [r-feature-four-ways], which calls for the same capability to be reachable from the MCP surface as well as CLI/JSON.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/reporting.py:309

chunk_findings.detail: The secret-correction test only inspects `--history` and `--json`; it never runs the default `ddflow show T1` output. If `show` prints the corrected `body` field verbatim for a `--secret` correction while the `--json` and `--history` renderers redact it, this test still passes, so it does not enforce the acceptance rule that a secret correction must never show the secret from the verb a person uses.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_show_corrected_fields.py:test_a_secret_correction_shows_the_marker_and_no_values

chunk_findings.detail: The new `history` flag is declared `cli_only=True`, so the MCP/JSON surface generated from this declared action cannot request correction history. A client that calls the MCP `show` action with `history=true` (or expects the same `ddflow show --history` capability through the declared API) gets `a.get("history")` absent/false, so the call lambda passes `history=False` to `A.show`; the view then only prints the latest correction per field and never the full correction list. That makes the history capability CLI-only, violating the four-way/record-parity acceptance that the same show capability is available in MCP and JSON, not only in the CLI. [r-feature-four-ways]
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/reporting.py:304

chunk_findings.detail: The `--secret` test only checks `--history` and `--json`; it never runs the default `show` output. For input `correct T1 --field body --text SECRET --reason ... --secret`, an implementation can redact the correction history and JSON while still printing the current `body` value in the normal markdown report, so `SECRET` is visible on the primary `show` surface, yet the test passes because it only asserts `SECRET not in --json + --history`. The test also loops over `data["corrections"][0]["fields"]` without asserting that list is non-empty, so an empty JSON `fields` array would also pass despite the acceptance requirement that corrected fields be exposed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_show_corrected_fields.py:85

chunk_findings.detail: The test named “appear only when the knobs are on” only tests the knob-on case: it enables `correct_digest_new` and asserts `row["new"]` is truthy. No test runs a non-secret correction with the default knobs and asserts that `row["old"]` and `row["new"]` are empty. Given an implementation that ignores `correct_digest_new` and always emits a digest, the suite still passes: `test_show_prints_author_model_and_the_corrected_marker` only checks that the raw old value is absent, and `test_json_adds_fields_and_keeps_the_existing_ones` never inspects `fields`, so the “only when the knobs are on” requirement is not actually verified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_show_corrected_fields.py:91

chunk_findings.detail: The MCP test only asserts `author_model` and `corrections[0]["reason"]`. An MCP `show` result that omits `by`, `at`, or `fields` (or returns an empty `fields` list) still passes, while the acceptance criterion says the same correction fields must appear in the MCP action. Given a response containing `{"author_model": "model-right", "corrections": [{"reason": "fix"}]}`, the test passes even though the MCP surface is missing the marker fields required by `r-record-parity`-style parity.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_show_corrected_fields.py:150

chunk_findings.detail: The updated secret-redaction test still does not prove that `--secret` JSON output omits the old value or its digest. It removes the earlier assertion that the full `--json` output lacks `SECRET` and `"first body"`, and now only checks `new_text not in json.dumps(data["corrections"])` plus that each correction field row has empty `old`/`new`. data.body: REC-show-corrected-fields made ddflow show (task, phase, bug, research) read back record.corrected. The same corrections can be written for a lesson, decision, memory or session (ddflow correct), whose own show verbs still print none of it. Reuse api/reporting/records.py _corrections and views/markdown/report.py correction_lines; additive JSON field corrections; test per kind. Found while hunting bugs in REC-show-corrected-fields.

chunk_findings.detail: The `--secret` test only checks `--history` and `--json`; it never runs the default `show` output. For input `correct T1 --field body --text SECRET --reason ... --secret`, an implementation can redact the correction history and JSON while still printing the current `body` value in the normal markdown report, so `SECRET` is visible on the primary `show` surface, yet the test passes because it only asserts `SECRET not in --json + --history`. The test also loops over `data["corrections"][0]["fields"]` without asserting that list is non-empty, so an empty JSON `fields` array would also pass despite the acceptance requirement that corrected fields be exposed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_show_corrected_fields.py:85

chunk_findings.detail: The test named “appear only when the knobs are on” only tests the knob-on case: it enables `correct_digest_new` and asserts `row["new"]` is truthy. No test runs a non-secret correction with the default knobs and asserts that `row["old"]` and `row["new"]` are empty. Given an implementation that ignores `correct_digest_new` and always emits a digest, the suite still passes: `test_show_prints_author_model_and_the_corrected_marker` only checks that the raw old value is absent, and `test_json_adds_fields_and_keeps_the_existing_ones` never inspects `fields`, so the “only when the knobs are on” requirement is not actually verified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_show_corrected_fields.py:91

chunk_findings.detail: The MCP test only asserts `author_model` and `corrections[0]["reason"]`. An MCP `show` result that omits `by`, `at`, or `fields` (or returns an empty `fields` list) still passes, while the acceptance criterion says the same correction fields must appear in the MCP action. Given a response containing `{"author_model": "model-right", "corrections": [{"reason": "fix"}]}`, the test passes even though the MCP surface is missing the marker fields required by `r-record-parity`-style parity.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_show_corrected_fields.py:150

chunk_findings.detail: The secret-redaction test no longer exercises a secret corrected value. The previous code corrected `body` to `SECRET`; this version corrects it to `"[redacted]"` but still asserts only that `SECRET` is absent from the outputs. Because `SECRET` is no longer supplied as the correction value, the `SECRET not in out` assertions are vacuous for the value under test. If `show`, `show --history`, or `--json` leaks the current corrected body value, the test still passes since the body is `[redacted]`; a real `--secret` correction containing a secret would not be caught.
